text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Wednesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- 70-year-old conservative MP Romualdas Sikorskis, who suffered a brain haemmorage in November has been partially paralysed and will not be able to return to work, doctors say.

- A member of parliament of the Radical group Young Lithuania demanded on Tuesday the resignation of the interior minister and the prosecutor general, who he says are totally incapable of coping with the difficult crime situation in the northern town of Panevezhys.
- Criminals in the second city of Kaunas brought themselves to witness against suspected underworld mob leader Henrikas Daktaras.

- The 10 biggest beer breweries produced 112.5 million litres of beer, four percent more than in 1995. The leaders of the market are Utenos gerimai with 39.5 million litres, Kalnapilis with 24.4 million litres and Svyturus with 17.4 million litres.
- Lithuanian lawmakers decided to form a temporary commission to investigate whether MPs and council officials collaborated with the secret services of foreign countries, meaning Russia.
- Interior Minister Vidmantas Ziemelis told parliament that attempts are being made to hinder his work in rooting out organised crime.
- The interest rate for three month government T-bills dropped below 10 percent for the first time this year and was 9.62 percent.

- The former head of the pro-Soviet militia OMON, Boleslovas Makutinovicius, who actively participated in the January 13 hardline crackdown in Vilnius now leads a private security company in Moscow and has not lost hope of marching in the streets of Vilnius some day.
